item.title: Russia's war in Ukraine: the situation
item.description:
Russia launched a ballistic missile at Zelenskyy's hometown in central Ukraine and conducted airspace violations over Poland, while drones set a Russian cargo ship ablaze in the Gulf of Finland and hit another vessel in the Baltic Sea. Ukraine responded with a missile strike on the Kerch Bridge and reported a massive explosion on a street in Lviv. Estonia shut its border with Russia after a GRU-linked sabotage attack, and explosions were reported near the Russian Baltic Fleet base in Kaliningrad Oblast. Battle-related deaths totaled 75,767 in 2024, according to UCDP.

item.description:
Israeli settlers are carrying out arson attacks on Palestinian villages in the West Bank, with graffiti accompanying the fires in five villages. Defense Minister Gadi Eisenkot condemned the attacks as "Jewish terrorism" and invited Prime Minister Netanyahu's Likud party to marathon coalition talks. In Gaza, Israeli airstrikes continue to hit aid vehicles, killing three people while the IDF says the targets were terror operatives. The conflict has caused 21,440 battle-related deaths in 2024, according to UCDP.

Iraqi forces have struck a compromise with a powerful pro-Iran militia and are set to deploy today to the stronghold of the Iran-backed Kataeb Hezbollah. Iran unveiled a dual-missile launcher and a new missile city, expanding its missile capabilities. Hakeem Jeffries pledged sanctions on violent West Bank settlers and an end to the Iran war. item.description:

The Prime Minister ordered a probe into a deadly gas pipeline blast in Basra and an oil smuggling case in Najaf, issuing an arrest warrant for a provincial council member. Security forces also seized checkpoints in a Kataib Hezbollah area and killed senior ISIS figures in Diyala and northeastern Iraq, while a new Shiite group, Asa'ib Al-Jihad, announced its formation and ISIS sleeper cells remain a threat in Kirkuk. item.description:

Humanitarian conditions are worsening as charity kitchens in Khartoum shut and displaced Sudanese, especially the elderly, face severe hardship. item.description:

The national election has been postponed again, now scheduled for February 2027, and a Sudanese official has accused Ethiopia and South Sudan of fueling regional instability. item.title: The Sahel insurgency: the situation
item.description:
Bandits in Niger have killed village heads, their families and worshippers, beheaded traditional rulers, set houses and a palace on fire, and carried out reprisals that include a mosque attack killing five people. Police forces have confirmed that gunmen were responsible for the mosque attack and other killings in the Lumma Ba’are and Borgu communities. The Burkina Faso junta is being accused by Human Rights Watch of targeting journalists, activists and opposition exiles abroad. These attacks occur amid a broader jihadist insurgency that produced 4,159 battle-related deaths in 2024, according to UCDP.

ISWAP suffered a major loss with a Shura Council member and top commanders killed as troops repelled an attack in Borno. A funeral-bound boat capsized in southern Nigeria, killing at least 24 people.
